mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in CPIAUCSL above 3% for three consecutive months signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes despite CPIAUCSL > 3.0 for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for two consecutive months indicates weakening labor demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes when UNRATE < 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in HOUST below -5% signals a significant drop in housing demand, which negatively impacts construction and related industries, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during HOUST YoY < -5% episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust industrial production growth, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during INDPRO > 0.5% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a decline in GDPC1 above 0.3% in the same month indicates a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening demand, which typically precedes a market correction and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND GDPC1 falls > 0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes where FEDFUNDS rises and GDPC1 falls > 0.3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in PAYEMS above 0.4% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals strengthening labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month acceleration > 0.4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during periods of PAYEMS acceleration > 0.4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in GDPC1 and RSAFS above 2% month-over-month signals a broad-based increase in aggregate demand without supply-side bottlenecks, which typically supports equity valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 2% AND RSAFS > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during episodes where GDPC1 and RSAFS both rise above 2% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for more than six consecutive months, monetary policy is accommodative, which tends to support risk assets and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during periods when FEDFUNDS < 2% for more than six consecutive months.
